gaps.title: Vast last-mile network for a product with zero tolerance for a cold break
gaps.detail: Vadilal moves product through roughly 23 C&FA, 500+ distributors, and 40,000+ retail outlets -- and ice cream is a product where a cold-chain break doesn't stay hidden, it visibly melts. Nothing in available research names a monitoring system covering that last-mile network at this scale.
gaps.gnd_service: Cold Chain Management (ThinxFresh) + Asset Tracking & Monitoring
gaps.based_on: Vadilal operates a Cold Chain Network comprising three manufacturing plants... about 23 C&FA, more than 500 distributors, and over 40,000 retailers.

gaps.title: Three manufacturing plants across two states feeding one distribution network
gaps.detail: Product is produced across Pundhra and Dharampur in Gujarat and Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh before entering the same distribution web. Consistency of cold-chain monitoring standards across three separately located plants, before product even reaches distribution, is worth confirming rather than assuming.
gaps.based_on: Vadilal operates a Cold Chain Network comprising three manufacturing plants (Pundhra and Dharampur in Gujarat, and Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh).

pitch.angle: Vadilal moves nearly a quarter of India's entire ice cream market through 23 C&FA, 500+ distributors, and 40,000+ retail outlets -- a product where a single cold-chain break doesn't just risk compliance, it visibly melts on the shelf. Nothing in public materials names a monitoring system covering that last-mile network at this scale. GND's ThinxFresh gives Vadilal instant deviation alerts across the distribution web that actually determines whether a quarter of India's ice cream reaches customers still frozen.
pitch.opener: Moving a quarter of India's ice cream through 40,000+ retail outlets, how do you currently know if a cold-chain break happened before a customer does?
